THE FOLLOWING ARE FOUR BROAD PRIORITY AREAS THAT AGRILIFE RESEARCH FOCUSES ON: 1) DISCOVER NEW INNOVATIONS, TECHNOLOGIES, AND SCIENCE?BASED SOLUTIONS TO ENHANCE AGRICULTURAL AND ECOLOGICAL SYSTEMS, AND THE LIFE SCIENCES. 2) PROVIDE THE TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH NECESSARY TO DEVELOP AND PRODUCE HIGH?QUALITY, SAFE, AND SUSTAINABLE FOOD AND FIBER SYSTEMS WITH LOCAL, NATIONAL, AND GLOBAL IMPACTS. 3) ENHANCE THE EFFICIENCY, PROFITABILITY, AND RESILIENCY OF AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND FOOD SYSTEMS IN THE STATE OF TEXAS, ACROSS REGIONS AND THE WORLD. 4) DISCOVER, DISSEMINATE, AND FACILITATE THE ADOPTION OF SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE AT THE INTERSECTION OF NUTRITION, HUMAN HEALTH, AND AGRICULTURE. AGRILIFE RESEARCH ALLOCATES THESE HATCH MULTISTATE FUNDS THROUGHOUT THE AGENCY FOR THE RESEARCHERS TO CONDUCT THEIR RESEARCH AND GROW THEIR PROGRAMS. RESEARCHERS ARE EXPECTED TO PUBLISH THEIR RESULTS AND GROW THEIR RESEARCH PROGRAM THROUGH OTHER EXTERNAL SPONSORED RESEARCH PROJECTS. THE CITIZENS OF TEXAS, THE US AND THE WORLD BENEFIT FROM THE RESEARCH DONE BY THESE RESEARCHERS.

THROUGH INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS, NC STATE IS SOLVING CHALLENGES RELATED TO THE PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY OF BOTH LARGE- AND SMALL-SCALE FARMS. RESEARCHERS AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS ARE ALSO DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE LANDSCAPING AND GARDENING. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS ARE FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND METHODS FOR ANIMAL BREEDING, REPRODUCTION, NUTRITION, GENETICS AND GENOMICS, PHYSIOLOGY, ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS, PRODUCT QUALITY, AND HEALTH AND WELL-BEING. THESE INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS ALSO AIM TO TACKLE THE CRITICAL ISSUES IMPACTING THE QUALITY OF OUR SOIL, WATER AND AIR BY PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC SOLUTIONS FOR ANIMAL WASTE MANAGEMENT, WASTEWATER TREATMENT, NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT, SEPTIC SYSTEMS, WETLAND MANAGEMENT, SOIL PROPERTIES, AND FISHERY AND POND MANAGEMENT. NC STATE'S RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS TO ENHANCE FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH AND TO KEEP AMERICAN'S HEALTHY AND FREE FROM FOODBORNE ILLNESS NECESSITATE A FOCUS ON PREVENTING FOOD SAFETY PROBLEMS RATHER THAN TAKING A REACTIONARY APPROACH. NC STATE'S INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS FOCUS ON PROTECTING THE SAFETY OF FOODS ALONG THE ENTIRE SUPPLY CHAIN, FROM PRODUCTION TO CONSUMPTION. TO MEET THE GROWING  NEED FOR HEALTHY FOOD, RESEARCHERS ARE DEVELOPING AND PRODUCING NEW FOOD PRODUCTS THAT PROMOTE HEALTH AND PREVENT DISEASE. AT THE SAME TIME, EXTENSION PROVIDES NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMMING TO ENSURE THAT INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE THEY NEED TO MAKE INFORMED CHOICES ABOUT FOOD AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES. IMPROVING PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS: WITHIN THIS AREA, WE WILL WORK TO ADDRESS CROSS-CUTTING AND EMERGING ISSUES OF ANIMAL AND PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION. IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY THE EFFICIENCY OF DIFFERENT FEEDING SOURCES TO IMPROVE ANIMAL PRODUCTIVITY AND GUT HEALTH. IN PLANT SYSTEMS, THE FOCUS WILL BE IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE AND HIGH VALUE CROP PRODUCTION, SEASON EXTENSION, CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION, VALUE ADDED AGRICULTURE, DIGITAL AGRICULTURE, SOIL HEALTH, PEST CONTROL, AND AGRO ECONOMICS. EXTENSION WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND ITS WORK WITH LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS, PLACING SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON LIMITED RESOURCES, SMALL- SCALE MINORITY FARMERS. THE FARM PAVILION WILL FOCUS ON SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND LOCAL AND COMMUNITY FOOD SYSTEMS, HOUSING ITS APPLIED RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION PROGRAMS' STAFF AND PROVIDING SPACE FOR MEETINGS, FORUMS AND CONFERENCES.

THE OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY APPROVED PLAN OF WORK ENCOMPASSES A FIVE-YEAR PERIOD AND REPRESENTS A JOINT EFFORT BY THE TWO CRITICAL COMPONENTS OF OSU'S COLLEGE OF FOOD, AGRICULTURAL, AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES (CFAES), THE OHIO AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (OARDC) AND OSU EXTENSION. CFAES RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS ARE CONDUCTED IN NINE ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS ON OUR CAMPUSES IN COLUMBUS AND WOOSTER, ELEVEN RESEARCH STATIONS AND FIELD LABS, AND IN ALL 88 COUNTIES THROUGHOUT THE STATE. WHILE THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY IS THE LARGEST INDUSTRY IN THE BUCKEYE STATE, CFAES RESEARCH REACHES BEYOND AGRICULTURE AND COVERS ENVIRONMENTAL, WATER QUALITY AND SOCIETAL ISSUES THAT RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES FACE. CFAES RECENTLY UPDATED OUR STRATEGIC PLAN, INCLUDING THE GOALS LISTED BELOW TO GUIDE OUR WORK AND ACTIONS AT ALL LEVELS AND WITH INVOLVEMENT OF RESEARCH FACULTY IN ALL AREAS. GOAL 1 STUDENT/LEARNER FIRST PHILOSOPHY, CFAES TEACHING REACHES ACROSS THE LIFESPAN FROM YOUTH SERVED THROUGH 4-H PROGRAMS TO STUDENTS PURSUING DEGREES ON CAMPUS TO 2 MILLION PLUS LIFELONG LEARNERS IN EXTENSION PROGRAMS. GOAL 2 INNOVATIVE SCHOLARSHIP TO SUSTAIN LIFE, CFAES RESEARCH PROJECTS AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS ADDRESS OUR CRITICAL ISSUES WHICH COVER AREAS IN HEALTH AND WELLNESS, ECONOMIC VITALITY, FOOD SECURITY AND P RODUCTION, ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY AND SUSTAINABILITY AS WELL AS HELPING PEOPLE THRIVE ACROSS THE LIFESPAN. GOAL 3 CAPACITY BUILDING OF OUR PEOPLE AND OUR COMMUNITIES. PEOPLE ARE OUR GREATEST ASSET AND CFAES STRIVES TO BUILD ON THE SUCCESS OF OUR PEOPLE. CHANGING WORKFORCE DYNAMICS, COVID-19 PRESSURES, MARKET COMPETITION, ECONOMIC DRIVERS, AN INCREASING DESIRE FOR A MORE BALANCED APPROACH TO HOW LIFE AND WORK INTERFACE, AND A NEED FOR DIVERSIFYING OUR TALENT. GOAL 4 PARTNER OF CHOICE, CFAES WANTS TO ENGAGE OUR ENTIRE COMMUNITY, INCLUDING BOTH INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL STAKEHOLDERS. GOAL 5 RESOURCE STEWARDSHIP IN A ONE-COLLEGE MODEL, CFAES CONTINUES TO TRANSFORM AND IMPROVE OUR PHYSICAL ENVIRONMENT ACROSS OUR THREE CAMPUSES. A NEW SCIENCE BUILDING PROVIDING MODERN RESEARCH SPACE WAS RECENTLY COMPLETED ON THE WOOSTER CAMPUS AND THE NEW CONTROLLED ENVIRONMENT AGRICULTURE RESEARCH COMPLEX HAS RECENTLY OPENED AT WATERMAN FARM ON THE COLUMBUS CAMPUS. THE JOINT POW WAS DEVELOPED AROUND THESE GOALS AS WELL AS FIVE CRITICAL ISSUES. 1 HEALTH AND WELLNESS, EXPLORING HEALTH RELATED ISSUES INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO MENTAL HEALTH AWARENESS AND INITIATIVES, HEALTH INEQUITY, CHRONIC DISEASE AND OBESITY PREVENTION, COMMUNITY NUTRITION EDUCATION, AND FARM SAFETY. 2 ECONOMIC VITALITY, ISSUES RELATED TO ECONOMIC VITALITY INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO BUSINESS RETENTION AND EXPANSION, ENHANCING RURAL ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES, INCREASING BROADBAND ACCESS IN RURAL AREAS, THE EFFECTS OF TRADE POLICIES ON FOOD AND AG INDUSTRIES, AND THE ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF ECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT. 3 FOOD SECURITY AND PRODUCTION, WE WILL EXPLORE ISSUES RELATED TO MITIGATING FOOD INSECURITY THROUGH COMMUNITY SERVICE AND FOOD PRODUCTION EDUCATION PROGRAMS AND FOOD SYSTEM SUSTAINABILITY INCLUDING DIGITAL AGRICULTURE, CLIMATE SMART AGRICULTURE, IMPROVED FOOD ANIMAL HEALTH AND PRODUCTION, CROP IMPROVEMENT AND RESILIENCY, WEED AND PEST CONTROL, PLANT BREEDING AND DISEASE RESISTANCE, NUTRIENT DENSE FOODS, NEW FOOD PRESERVATIVES, AND ANTIMICROBIAL FOOD PACKAGING. 4 ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY AND SUSTAINABILITY. RESEARCH TOPICS COVER AREAS SUCH AS SOIL HEALTH AND REMEDIATION, BIOLOGICAL CONTROL AGENTS, REDUCTION OF PESTICIDE USE, SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION OF POLYMERS AND BIOPLASTICS, WATER QUALITY AND WASTEWATER TREATMENT, AQUATIC ECOSYSTEM HEALTH, AIR QUALITY AND SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION OF BIOPRODUCTS AND RENEWABLE FUELS. 5 THRIVING ACROSS THE LIFESPAN, PROGRAMS UNDER THIS CRITICAL ISSUE ARE RELATED TO POSITIVE HUMAN DEVELOPMENT FOR ALL AGES. A MAJOR FOCUS IS YOUTH DEVELOPMENT THROUGH 4-H AND FINANCIAL LITERACY PROGRAMS.

THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES AT PENN STATE WILL PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE SUPPORT TO THE RESIDENTS OF PENNSYLVANIA THROUGH THE A CTIVITIES OF THE PENNSYLVANIA AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (AES) AND PENN STATE EXTENSION (EXTENSION). WE WILL BE RESPONSIVE TO STAKEHOLDER NEEDS THROUGH TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH AND DELIVERY OF SCIENCE-BASED PROGRAMS TO CLIENTELE, BUT WE WILL ALSO CONDUCT REGION ALLY, NATIONALLY, AND INTERNATIONALLY RELEVANT FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH THAT GENERATES BASELINE DATA TO SOLVE FUTURE NEEDS RELATIVE TO AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND ACTIVELY SEEK NEW AND BETTER WAYS TO COMMUNICATE OUR PROGRAMS TO NEW AUDIENCES. OUR FACULTY AND STAFF, SUPPORTED BY FEDERAL BASE FUNDING (TO INCLUDE HATCH AND MULTISTATE HATCH FUNDS), WILL EFFECTIVELY LEVERAGE THIS INVESTMENT AGAINST MANY OTHER EXTERNAL FUNDING SOURCES TO CONDUCT PROGRAMS OF THE HIGHEST CALIBER. WE ARE COMMITTED TO EXCELLENCE IN RESEARCH, EDUCATING THE NEXT GENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS AND CITIZENS, AND PROMOTING LIFE-LONG LEARNING AMONG THE CITIZENS OF PENNSYLVANIA AND WITHIN THE REGION AND NATION. OUR MISSION IS CLEAR: THE MISSION OF THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES IS TO DISCOVER, INTEGRATE, TRANSLATE, AND DISSEMINATE KNOWLEDGE TO ENHANCE THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SYSTEM, NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP, AND ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL WELLBEING, THEREBY IMPROVING THE LIVES OF PEOPLE IN PENNSYLVANIA, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD. AGRICULTURE FACES CHALLENGES OF RISING ENERGY COSTS, WEATHER EXTREMES, AN EXPANDING HUMAN POPULATION, ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION, LOSS OF BIODIVERSITY, LABOR SHORTAGES, ARMED CONFLICT, AND A LINGERING PANDEMIC. TO HELP MEET THESE CHALLENGES, WE ARE DEVELOPING A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK BASED ON THE SCIENCE OF AGRICULTURAL SUSTAINABILITY, DEFINED AS THE INTEGRATION OF NATURAL AND SOCIAL SCIENCES TO INFORM PRACTICE AND POLICY FOR PRODUCTIVE, WORKING LANDSCAPES, HEALTHY WATERSHEDS, AND RESILIENT ECONOMIES. THIS INNOVATIVE APPROACH TO AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH, ENGAGEMENT, AND EDUCATION CENTERS ON THE IMPACTS AND SYNERGIES OF CONTIGUOUS RURAL AND URBAN LANDSCAPES. THIS MOSAIC OF DENSELY POPULATED AREAS NEXT TO FORESTS AND AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES IS UNIQUE TO PENNSYLVANIA AND THE MID-ATLANTIC REGION AND REQUIRES AN INTEGRATED STRATEGY TO ACHIEVE HEALTHY AND THRIVING AGRICULTURE, NATURAL SYSTEMS, ECONOMIES, AND COMMUNITIES. A PRIMARY COMPONENT OF AES AND EXTENSION WORK IN OUR COLLEGE WILL BE BUILT ON THE THREE INTEGRATED PILLARS OF INTENSIFICATION, RESILIENCE, AND REGENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES AS SOLUTIONS TO SOME OF THE MOST VEXING PROBLEMS CONFRONTING PENNSYLVANIA AND SIMILAR MOSAIC LANDSCAPES WORLDWIDE. WE WILL HOLISTICALLY AND COMPREHENSIVELY ADDRESS THESE CRITICAL ISSUES: INCREASING THE EFFICIENCY AND PROFITABILITY OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION WHILE MINIMIZING ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS AND IMPROVE HUMAN HEALTH, EQUIPPING FARMERS TO ABSORB AND RECOVER FROM SHORT-TERM EMERGENCIES AND LONG-TERM STRESSES TO THEIR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND LIVELIHOODS, OPTIMIZING PLANTS, ANIMALS, AND ECOSYSTEMS FOR RESILIENCE TO AND FASTER RECOVERY FROM ENVIRONMENTALLY RELATED STRESSES, DEVELOPING STRATEGIES FOR BETTER MANAGEMENT OF NUTRIENT INPUTS AND OUTPUTS ACROSS COMPLEX AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL RESOURCE SYSTEMS, FROM LOCAL FIELDS AND FARMS TO LARGE WATERSHEDS, HARNESSING SPATIAL DATA AND REMOTE SENSING TECHNOLOGIES TO MAP AND MODEL PREDICTIVE SIMULATIONS OF ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE.

THE ACES OFFICE OF RESEARCH AND AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION ENABLES AND ENCOURAGES FACULTY CREATIVITY, INNOVATION, AND INTERDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATION TO ADVANCE THE MISSION OF THE COLLEGE IN AN ENVIRONMENT THAT IS INCLUSIVE, RESPECTFUL OF DIVERSITY, AND OPEN AND EQUITABLE FOR ALL. WE ACCOMPLISH THIS THROUGH CAPACITY FUND INVESTMENTS IN SEED FUNDING, EQUIPMENT, RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE AND FACILITIES, TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES, AND STRATEGIC INITIATIVES ACROSS A BROAD SPECTRUM OF RESEARCH IN ALL ASPECTS OF AGRICULTURE. ACTIVITIES FOCUS ON FIVE CRITICAL ISSUES: COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT, INCLUSION <(>&<)> LEADERSHIP; ECONOMIC <(>&<)> WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT; SAFE, HEALTHY ENVIRONMENTS <(>&<)> BEHAVIORS; SAFE, PLENTIFUL, <(>&<)> ACCESSIBLE FOOD SUPPLY; AND THRIVING NATURAL RESOURCES. DELIVERABLES <(>&<)> OUTCOMES: COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT, INCLUSION, <(>&<)> LEADERSHIP- WE STUDY: PERCEPTIONS AND KNOWLEDGE OF EXTENSION EDUCATORS REGARDING AGING IN PLACE IN RURAL ILLINOIS; THE INFLUENCE OF INTERPERSONAL RELATIONSHIPS IN BLACK ADOLESCENTS WHO HAVE EXPERIENCED RACIAL DISCRIMINATION; INCLUSIVE CONSERVATION POLICY DEVELOPMENT APPROACHES. ECONOMIC <(>&<)> WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT- WE STUDY: AGRICULTURE AND RURAL MARKETS, INCLUDING ACCESS, PRICING AND TRADING DYNAMICS, AND MARKETS IN TRANSITION; LEGAL AND POLICY ISSUES AROUND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION, MARKETING TRADE, AND THE ENVIRONMENT; THE ECONOMIC AND POLICY IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGE; IMPROVING HIGHER EDUCATION ACCESS AND COMPLETION IN RURAL ILLINOIS; PREPARING POSTSECONDARY STUDENTS FOR CAREERS IN AGRICULTURE AND HUMAN SCIENCES; CREATING SUSTAINABLE, INCLUSIVE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR RURAL POPULATIONS. SAFE, HEALTHY ENVIRONMENTS <(>&<)> BEHAVIORS- WE STUDY: IMPROVING FOOD PRACTICES FOR RURAL ILLINOISIANS WHO LIVE ALONE; HOW ECONOMIC UNCERTAINTY AND DISADVANTAGED NEIGHBORHOODS INFLUENCE CHILD DEVELOPMENT; THE TRANSITION TO WORKING FROM HOME BACK TO THE OFFICE FOR MINORITY POPULATIONS AND WOMEN; THE ROLE OF SOCIAL NETWORKS FOR WOMEN'S WELL-BEING IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES; ADOLESCENT PEER STRESS AND BIOECOLOGICAL PROCESSES; PRENATAL DEVELOPMENT DURING MATERNAL INFLUENZA INFECTION; THERMALLY ABUSED OILS AND BREAST CANCER METASTASIS; NITRATE SOURCES AND CYCLING IN TILE-DRAINED FIELDS; COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS FOR RAPID CHARACTERIZATION AND QUANTIFICATION OF SOIL CLAY FRACTIONS. SAFE, PLENTIFUL, <(>&<)> ACCESSIBLE FOOD SUPPLY- WE STUDY: MAIZE OPTIMIZATION FOR INCREASED PHOTOSYNTHESIS AND WATER-USE EFFICIENCY; DEVELOPING MORE PROFITABLE WHEAT VARIETIES; DEVELOPING A NEW GENERATION OF CROP YIELD MONITORING SYSTEMS; REPRODUCTIVE PERFORMANCE IN RUMINANTS; THE BALANCE OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTIVITY AND SUSTAINABILITY BY USING UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS APPLICATIONS AND ENGINEERING TECHNIQUES; THE USE OF INSECTIVOROUS BATS TO CONTROL CROP PESTS; GENOMIC SELECTION AND GENOME-WIDE STUDIES FOR ILLINOIS CROP BREEDING PROGRAMS; IMPROVING DAIRY FARM BREEDING. THRIVING NATURAL RESOURCES- WE STUDY: CREATING CO-SUSTAINABILITY OF FOOD PRODUCTION WITH ADVANCED MODELING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE; A PARADIGM FOR FOOD AND BIOENERGY PRODUCTION AND WASTEWATER REUSE BASED ON BIOWASTE; RENEWABLE ENERGY USES IN ANIMAL FACILITIES; THE ECOLOGICAL CONSTRAINTS TO ACHIEVING SUSTAINABLE FISHERIES MANAGEMENT; MANAGEMENT AND POLICY CHALLENGES IN A WATER-SCARCE WORLD; ENVIRONMENTAL DNA SURVEILLANCE FOR INVASIVE SPECIES; THE EFFECTIVENESS OF WATER TREATMENT TECHNOLOGIES TO REMOVE PATHOGENS. BENEFICIARIES: WE SEEK TO IDENTIFY DIVERSE GROUPS AND INDIVIDUALS WHO CAN PROVIDE INPUT TO ENSURE THAT OUR PROGRAMS REMAIN SOCIALLY RELEVANT. THESE GROUPS INCLUDE STUDENTS (THE NEXT GENERATION OF PROFESSIONALS, SCIENTISTS AND EDUCATORS), FELLOW RESEARCHERS AND EXTENSION SPECIALISTS, GROWERS, COMMODITY GROUPS, COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, LAWMAKERS, AND INDUSTRY REPRESENTATIVES. WE SEEK TO IDENTIFY STAKEHOLDERS IN ILLINOIS FOCUSING ON LOCAL ISSUES, AND BEYOND THE STATE FOCUSING ON ISSUES OF REGIONAL OR NATIONAL CONCERN. THE AES DOES NOT EXPECT ANY SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES.

HATCH CAPACITY GRANT FUNDS ARE USED TO CONDUCT RESEARCH ACROSS DISCIPLINES IN AGRICULTURE, FOOD, ANIMAL AND HUMAN HEALTH TO ADVANCE PRODUCTION AND PROVIDE AN ADEQUATE AND NUTRITIOUS FOOD SUPPLY AND OPTIMIZE THE SOCIAL FABRIC OF FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES. CONTINUING DEMOGRAPHIC CHANGES, GLOBALIZATION AND TECHNOLOGICAL INNOVATIONS CREATE ONGOING OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES TOWARD ACHIEVING SOCIALLY BENEFICIAL, ECONOMICALLY SUCCESSFUL, AND ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND SYSTEMS FOR FOOD, FEED, FIBER, FUEL, AND OTHER VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS. IOWA STATE UNIVERSITY (ISU) HAS IDENTIFIED SIX LONG-TERM CRITICAL ISSUES THAT OUR RESEARCH PROJECTS ARE DESIGNED TO ADDRESS. FOOD PRODUCTION AND AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS: ISU SCIENTISTS ARE DEVELOPING NEW APPROACHES AND IMPROVING CURRENT STRATEGIES THAT MITIGATE PEST AND WEED DAMAGE TO AGRONOMIC PRODUCTS, CREATE DISEASE AND CLIMATE-RESISTANT CROPS, ENHANCE FOOD-ANIMAL PRODUCTION EFFICIENCIES, REDUCE BIOPRODUCT WASTE STREAMS FROM AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION, AND PREDICT WEATHER AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGES. STUDYING ANIMAL HEALTH AND WELFARE WILL IMPROVE ANIMAL LIFE QUALITY, AND INVESTIGATING ENVIRONMENTAL REGULATION ON ANIMAL PRODUCTIVITY WILL IMPROVE THE PHYSIOLOGICAL REGULATION OF REPRODUCTIVE EFFICIENCY IN DOMESTIC ANIMALS. NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP: ISU RESEARCHERS ARE DEVELOPING TOOLS AND STRATEGIES THAT CONSERVE NATURAL RESOURCES AND PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT, AND IDENTIFY FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH DISEASE THAT WILL ENHANCE THE MANAGEMENT AND CONSERVATION OF WILDLIFE POPULATIONS AND PROTECT HUMAN HEALTH. SOIL FERTILITY RESEARCH IS BEING CONDUCTED TO UNDERSTAND UNDERLYING PROCESSES THAT INFLUENCE SOIL ACIDIFICATION, CROP PHOSPHORUS AND POTASSIUM NEEDS AND UPTAKE, REMOVAL WITH HARVEST AND RECYCLING TO THE SOIL, AND TRANSPORT OFF FIELD, AS WELL AS EFFICIENT METHODS OF NUTRIENT OR AM ENDMENTS APPLICATION. HEALTH, NUTRITION, AND WELL-BEING: ISU RESEARCHERS ARE STUDYING WAYS TO IMPROVE HUMAN HEALTH THROUGH INFORMING CONSUMERS ABOUT NUTRITION AND LIFESTYLE APPROACHES, AND DEVELOPMENT OF A FOOD SYSTEM THAT IS COST-EFFICIENT AND PROMOTES HEALTH. SCIENTISTS ARE CONDUCTING STUDIES TO IDENTIFY NEW TARGETS THAT COULD STRENGTHEN THE IMMUNE SYSTEM TO PREVENT INFECTIOUS DISEASES TO IMPROVE WELL-BEING OF ANIMALS, PREVENT ZOONOTIC DISEASES THAT IMPACT HUMANS AND REDUCE THE CHANCES OF FUTURE OUTBREAKS. OTHER WORK IS IDENTIFYING NOVEL GENES IMPORTANT FOR OPTIMAL IMMUNE FUNCTION TO ALLOW GENETIC SELECTION OF THEREBY STRENGTHENING THE PRODUCTIVITY OF DOMESTICATED ANIMALS. HUMAN POTENTIAL AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, AND COMMUNITY AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT: ISU SCIENTISTS ARE WORKING TO ENHANCE THE RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION OF STUDENTS INTO AGRICULTURAL FIELDS TO ENSURE A SUSTAINABLE WORKFORCE. PROJECTS FOCUS ON FAMILIES AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE AND SUSTAINABILITY AND OPTIMIZING QUALITY OF LIFE ACROSS THE LIFESPAN. TRANSFORMATIVE TECHNOLOGY: ISU RESEARCHERS ARE DEVELOPING MACHINE SYSTEMS TO SUSTAINABLY INTENSIFY AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION TO MEET THE FOOD NEEDS OF GROWING GLOBAL DEMAND. OVERALL, THE RESEARCH WILL IMPROVE THE MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY OF AGRARIAN AND INTENSIVELY MANAGED LANDSCAPES AND CONTRIBUTE TO BROADER SOCIETALLY RELEVANT OUTCOMES THAT INCLUDE INCREASED ECONOMIC COMPETITIVENESS OF THE US AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISE. TARGET AUDIENCES AND OUTCOMES: THESE PROJECTS ARE OF HIGH VALUE TO A WIDE RANGE OF AUDIENCES. INFORMATION FROM THIS RESEARCH IS WIDELY DISSEMINATED THROUGH MANY OUTLETS. OUR GOAL IS TO BUILD THE CAPACITY OF ISU'S RESEARCH PROGRAMS TO MEET THE DEMANDS OF AGRICULTURE WHILE ENSURING QUALITY OF LIFE FOR CITIZENS, BUILDING PRODUCTIVE COMMUNITIES, PROTECTING NATURAL RESOURCES AND THE ENVIRONMENT, APPLYING TECHNOLOGY APPROPRIATELY AND EFFECTIVELY, AND GENERATING NEW KNOWLEDGE. ISU RESEARCHERS STRIVE TO OPTIMIZE THE USE OF CAPACITY FUNDS THROUGH THEIR RESEARCH BY ADDRESSING RELEVANT AND CRITICAL ISSUES FOR OUR STATE, OUR NATION AND THE WORLD.

positiveFlows.title: THE MISSION OF MSU AGBIORESEARCH IS TO ENGAGE IN INNOVATIVE, LEADING?EDGE RESEARCH THAT COMBINES SCIENTIFIC EXPERTISE WITH PRACTICAL EXPERIENCE TO GENERATE ECONOMIC PROSPERITY, SUSTAIN NATURAL RESOURCES, AND ENHANCE THE QUALITY OF LIFE IN MICHIGAN, THE NATION AND THE WORLD. AS WE OFTEN DESCRIBE AS FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH WITH AN INTENDED OUTCOME. ALL OF OUR RESEARCH IS AIMED AT SOLVING PROBLEMS OR CREATING A NEW OPPORTUNITY. THE 340 PLUS RESEARCHERS ACROSS CAMPUS STRIVE TO MAINTAIN A BALANCE BETWEEN BASIC AND APPLIED RESEARCH AND RELY HEAVILY ON THE INPUT OF THEIR CONSTITUENTS IN IDENTIFYING RESEARCH PRIORITIES. WITH HATCH FUNDING, WE WILL: INCREASE FARMERS' SUCCESS WITH PROTECTING THE ENVIRONMENT, ENSURING FOOD SAFETY, REACHING NEW MARKETS, AND ADVANCING AGRICULTURE THROUGH APPLIED RESEARCH; CONDUCT RESEARCH ON SELECTING PLANTS AND ANIMALS WITH DESIRABLE TRAITS AND ON NEW METHODS TO COMBAT DISEASES AND PARASITES; STUDY NUTRITION AND ANIMAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS; DEVELOP INTEGRATED CROP AND SOIL MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS TO MEET PRODUCTION AND ENVIRONMENTAL GOALS; ENHANCE THE PRODUCTION AND PROFITABILITY OF SMALL?SCALE AGRICULTURE PROJECTS AND IMPROVE COMMUNITY WELLNESS; USE EDUCATIONAL PROCESSES TO FACILITATE THE INCORPORATION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY INTO HOUSEHOLDS, GOVERNMENTAL OFFICES, AND BUSINESSES; INCREASE THE CAPACITY TO DEVELOP FOREST AND AGRICULTURAL?BASED RENEWABLE RESOURCES IN ECOLOGICALLY AND ECONOMICALLY SUSTAINABLE WAYS.

PURDUE'S COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE'S 2021-2026 STRATEGIC PLAN OUTLINES THE VISION AND MISSION: TO EMBODY THE IDEAL OF A CONTEMPORARY LAND-GRANT MISSION TO PREPARE TOMORROW'S LEADERS FOR MEETING SOCIETY'S NEEDS, AND TO ACHIEVE WORLDWIDE LEADERSHIP IN GROWING A SUSTAINABLE FUTURE BY ADDRESSING CHALLENGES IN FOOD, LIFE AND NATURAL RESOURCE SCIENCES, WORKING ACROSS DISCIPLINES. HATCH FUNDING FROM THE USDA NATIONAL INSTITUTE FOR FOOD AND AGRICULTURE (NIFA) ENABLES PURDUE'S COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE (COA) TO ACCOMPLISH ITS STRATEGIC PLAN THROUGH A BROAD PORTFOLIO OF RESEARCH ACROSS THREE UNITS ON THE WEST LAFAYETTE CAMPUS. PURDUE FACULTY IN THE COA, COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE, AND SELECTED DEPARTMENTS IN THE COLLEGE OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SCIENCES WHO HAVE RESEARCH APPOINTMENTS FUNDED AT 20% OR MORE BY FORMULA FUNDS ARE REQUIRED TO SUBMIT A FIVE-YEAR PLAN OF RESEARCH. THESE HATCH PROJECTS INCLUDE BOTH FIELD- AND LABORATORY-BASED RESEARCH (FUNDAMENTAL AND APPLIED) THAT DIRECTLY CONNECT WITH CRITICAL ISSUES CREATED TO INCORPORATE COA INITIATIVES, AND TO ALIGN WITH PRIORITIES OF NIFA, RESEARCH, EDUCATION <(>&<)> ECONOMIC GOALS OF USDA, AGRICULTURE <(>&<)> FOOD RESEARCH INITIATIVE, FOUNDATION FOR FOOD <(>&<)> AGRICULTURE RESEARCH, AND EXTENSION COMMITTEE ON ORGANIZATION <(>&<)> POLICY. CRITICAL ISSUES ARE CLIMATE CHANGE, NATURAL RESOURCES AND THE ENVIRONMENT, AND SUSTAINABLE ENERGY; WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT; POSITIVE YOUTH DEVELOPMENT AND 4-H OPPORTUNITIES; BIG DATA, INTERNET OF THINGS, BROADBAND ACCESS, DIGITAL LITERACY, INCLUSION, AND INNOVATION; HUMAN, FAMILY, AND COMMUNITY HEALTH; FOOD PRODUCTION, SECURITY, AND SAFETY; AND URBAN AGRICULTURE AND URBAN EXTENSION. HOWEVER, THESE RESOURCES ARE EXPERIENCING INCREASED PRESSURE BECAUSE OF SEVERAL BIOTIC AND ABIOTIC STRESSORS. WE SEEK TO INITIATE CUTTING EDGE INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH RELATED TO CLIMATE CHANGE, ECOSYSTEM HEALTH AND RESTORATION, SOIL HEALTH, WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY, ENVIRONMENTAL CHEMISTRY, HABITAT EVALUATION, NATURE-BASED RECREATION, VALUING ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, GREEN TECHNOLOGY INCLUDING ALTERNATIVE AND SUSTAINABLE ENERGY, SUSTAINABLE LANDSCAPES, ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATICS AMONG OTHERS. (3) THE HEALTH OF EARTH'S ECOSYSTEMS HAS DETERIORATED SO MUCH THAT THE PUBLIC IS CONCERNED ABOUT A LOSS OF LIFE SUPPORT FOR ALL ORGANISMS. ECOSYSTEM HEALTH INCLUDES BOTH THE BIOPHYSICAL AND SOCIOECOLOGICAL DIMENSIONS. THE BIOPHYSICAL REALM INCLUDES CLIMATE, AIR, THE ENVIRONMENT, WATER, ENERGY, WILDLIFE, FOOD, SOIL HEALTH AMONG OTHERS. THE SOCIOECONOMIC ASPECTS INCLUDE ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY, SOCIAL SERVICES, RECREATION AND HUMAN AND ANIMAL HEALTH AND WELFARE. (4) MISSOURI IS AN AGRARIAN STATE SUPPORTING A $93.7 BILLION AGRICULTURE INDUSTRY. OVER THE NEXT DECADE, THE AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND FORESTRY INDUSTRIES IN MISSOURI ARE PROJECTED TO GENERATE 13,000 JOB OPENINGS ANNUALLY. TECHNOLOGICAL ADVANCES, INCLUDING SMART FARMS AND BIG DATA AND DATA ANALYTICS, HAVE CREATED SEVERAL NEW JOB OPPORTUNITIES. HOWEVER, FINDING SKILLED LABOR CONTINUES TO BE A CHALLENGE. WE SEEK TO PROVIDE HANDS-ON TRAINING THROUGH BASIC AND APPLIED RESEARCH RELATED TO AGRICULTURE PRODUCTION AND PROCESSING, FOOD AND NUTRITION, NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, AND AGRIBUSINESS AND AGRICULTURAL POLICY THAT WILL PRODUCE A WELL-TRAINED WORKFORCE FOR THE AGRICULTURE INDUSTRY OF THE PRESENT AND FUTURE AND FURTHER THE ECONOMIC IMPACT OF AGRICULTURE. DELIVERABLES AND OUTCOMES: THIS PROJECT WILL GENERATE SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE THAT WILL ADVANCE AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND NATURAL RESOURCES FOR A HEALTHY FUTURE; BETTER CROPS AND CROPPING SYST EMS THAT WILL BE RESILIENT TO CHANGING CLIMATE AND EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS; BETTER UNDERSTANDING AND QUANTIFICATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL BENEFITS AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES OF SUSTAINABLE AND REGENERATIVE CROPPING; AND, ECONOMIC AND POLICY ANALYSIS THAT CAN HELP FARMERS/R ANCHERS/POLICY MAKERS MAKE APPROPRIATE DECISIONS. ALL THE ABOVE OUTCOMES WILL ALSO GENERATE PEER REVIEWED PUBLICATIONS, GRADUATE THESES AND DISSERTATIONS, PROFESSIONAL PRESENTATIONS, DEMONSTRATION TRIALS, NEW VARIETIES, INVENTION DISCLOSURES AND PATENTS AND DATA AND MATERIALS. BENEFICIARIES: THE DIRECT INTENDED BENEFICIARIES ARE FARMERS AND RANCHERS IN MISSOURI PRIMARILY, BUT OVERALL, IT BENEFITS THE CITIZENS OF THE STATE. SUBRECIPIENTS: N/A

TENNESSEE'S TWO LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS COMPRISE THE TENNESSEE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SYSTEM. THEY WORK INDEPENDENTLY AND COLLABORATIVELY TO CONDUCT RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ALL 95 COUNTIES AND TO SERVE THE STATE'S 6.9 MILLION PEOPLE. TENNESSEE'S LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS CONDUCT RESEARCH AND PROVIDE OUTREACH IN FIVE KEY AREAS TO ADDRESS CRITICAL ISSUES AFFECTING THE STATE: SUPPORTING FOOD, FIBER, AND ENERGY SYSTEMS; ENHANCING BIODIVERSITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY; ENRICHING OUR ECONOMY; DEVELOPING OUR WORKFORCE; AND STRENGTHENING OUR HEALTH. EXTENSION WILL CONTINUE TO PROVIDE PROGRAMS TO ADDRESS THE ONGOING NEEDS OF CITIZENS AND AGRICULTURE PRODUCERS ACROSS THE STATE. HEALTH ISSUES ARE A TOP CONCERN FOR RESIDENTS. EXTENSION WILL STRENGTHEN HEALTH PROGRAMMING BY OFFERING THE HEALTH AND NUTRITION PROGRAMS AND PROVIDE RESOURCES FOR IMPROVING DIETARY AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY FOR LIMITED-RESOURCE TENNESSEANS. EXTENSION LIVESTOCK AND FORAGE PROGRAMS STRENGTHEN THE STATE'S LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS THOUGH RESEARCH AND OUTREACH IN HAY SCHOOLS, LATE GESTATION NUTRITION, MARKETING, AND FORAGES. TENNESSEE EXTENSION HAS DEVELOPED PROGRAMS TO STRENGTHEN AND PROVIDE VALUE-ADDED OPPORTUNITIES AND PROGRAMS ON FARM FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT. THE CONSUMER ECONOMICS PROGRAM HELPS FAMILIES INCREASE SAVINGS, DECREASE DEBT, AND FINANCIALLY PLAN. 4-H WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS ARE DESIGNED FOR YOUTH TO PROVIDE NEEDED SKILLS, TRAINING, AND EXPERIENCES TO PARTICIPANTS. EXTENSION CONTINUES TO DEVELOP PROGRAMS TO ENCOURAGE AND PROVIDE YOUTH DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES. UT AGRESEARCH CONDUCTS RESEARCH WITHIN EIGHT ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS AND SEVEN PHYSICAL CENTERS, AND AT TEN AGRESEARCH AND EDUCATION CENTERS (REC) LOCATED THROUGHOUT THE STATE. IN ADDITION TO A DECADE OF EXCELLENCE: TEN-YEAR STRATEGIC PLAN FOR UTIA, 2018-2028, AGRESEARCH OPERATES UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF ITS 2021-2024 AGRESEARCH STRATEGIC ACTION PLAN (ASAP) WITH THE OBJECTIVES TO BALANCE A PORTFOLIO OF INTEGRATED, INTER-DISCIPLINARY PROGRAMS, CULTIVATE TEAMS TO APPROACH COMPLEX PROBLEMS, ADVANCE CONCEPTS WITH STRUCTURED SUPPORT, AND TO ENSURE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT CAPACITY WITH TARGETED INVESTMENT. AGRESEARCH IS EMPHASIZING FOUR PROGRAMMATIC THEMES TO ESTABLISH INTEGRATED PROGRAMS THAT CONTRIBUTE SOLUTIONS TO COMPLEX PROBLEMS. THE UT ONE HEALTH INITIATIVE, A UT SYSTEM-WIDE APPROACH HOUSED WITHIN AGRESEARCH, IS WORKING TO PRESERVE AND PROMOTE HUMAN, ANIMAL, PLANT, AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH TO ADVANCE ECONOMIC GROWTH, AND CONSERVE BIODIVERSITY AT LOCAL, NATIONAL, AND GLOBAL SCALES. SCHOLARS FROM ACROSS AGRESEARCH ARE CONTRIBUTING TO STUDIES THAT DEFINE THE FACTORS THREATENING HUMAN AND ANIMAL HEALTH, AND THE HEALTH OF OUR ENVIRONMENT. THE EMERGING DIGITAL AGRICULTURE PROGRAM DRAWS ON THE SKILLS OF RESEARCHERS ACROSS UT TO CREATE A TRANSDISCIPLINARY PATH TO CARBONSMART AGRICULTURE AND BENEFITS FROM ONGOING INVESTMENT TO BUILD CAPACITY IN PRECISION LIVESTOCK FARMING (PLF). THE PROGRAM INCORPORATES BOTH PLANT AND ANIMAL MANAGEMENT PROJECTS THAT ULTIMATELY WILL CONTRIBUTE INFORMATION TO REFINE STRATEGIES THAT OFFER CARBON REDUCTIONS OVER TODAY'S AGRICULTURE SYSTEMS. AGRESEARCH IS REALIGNING THE CAPABILITIES AT ITS REC'S TO SUPPORT THE PLF INITIATIVE, INCLUDING THE INSTALLATION OF A ROBOTIC MILKING SYSTEM. THE TRANSFORMATIONAL AGRICULTURAL GENOMICS AND SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY PROGRAM WILL ADVANCE ANIMAL AND PLANT-BASED PRODUCTIVITY AND RESILIENCE. ALTHOUGH EARLY IN ITS DEVELOPMENT, THE INITIATIVE ALREADY ENGAGES FACULTY ACROSS UT TO ADVANCE STATE-OF-THE-ART SCIENCE TO DESIGN CROPS THAT ARE RESILIENT TO CLIMATE CHANGE. THE BIOECONOMY ADVANCEMENT INITIATIVE IS AN ESTABLISHED INTERDISCIPLINARY, MULTIDEPARTMENTAL PROGRAM FOCUSED ON SUSTAINABLE FUELS, CHEMICALS, AND MATERIALS FROM STRANDED RESOURCES. THE INITIATIVE IS EMBRACING THE CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK OF THE CIRCULAR BIOECONOMY, SEEKING TO EXTEND THE LIFETIME OF RENEWABLE CARBON IN THE MARKETPLACE.

OUR STRATEGIC RESEARCH PLAN AIMS AT MAKING FUNDAMENTAL SCIENTIFIC DISC OVERIES AND APPLYING THEM TO CREATE NEW TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL ENHANCE THE SUSTAINABILITY AND RESILIENCE OF ADAPTIVE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS. positiveFlows.title: GEORGIA, ONE OF THE ORIGINAL 13 COLONIES, HAS A LAND AREA OF 57,701 SQUARE MILES AND A WATER AREA OF 1,706 SQUARE MILES, WHICH MAKES IT THE LARGEST STATE EAST OF THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER (21TH OVERALL). GEORGIA FALLS WITHIN FIVE MAJOR PHYSIOGRAPHIC REGIONS: THE BLUE RIDGE MOUNTAINS IN THE NORTHEAST; THE RIDGE AND VALLEY PROVINCE AND THE CUMBERLAND PLATEAU IN THE NORTHWEST; THE PIEDMONT ACROSS CENTRAL GEORGIA; AND THE COASTAL PLAIN IN THE SOUTH. ELEVATIONS RANGE FROM SEA LEVEL TO 4,784 FEET AT BRASSTOWN BALD IN THE BLUE RIDGE MOUNTAINS. THE 2020 CENSUS ESTIMATED GEORGIA'S POPULATION WAS 10,711,908 AND REPORTED 23.8% OF GEORGIANS ARE UNDER AGE 18 AND 13.9% ARE 65 OR OLDER. ACCORDING TO THE CENSUS,51.9% OF GEORGIANS IDENTIFY THEMSELVES AS WHITE/CAUCASIAN, 31% AS BLACK/AFRICAN-AMERICAN, 4.5% AS ASIAN,.5% AS AMERICAN INDIAN/ALASKA NATIVE, .1% AS NATIVE HAWAIIAN/PACIFIC ISLANDER, AND 6.9% AS MORE THAN ONE RACE. IT WAS ALSO REPORTED THAT 10.5% OF GEORGIANS IDENTIFY AS HISPANIC OR LATINO. GEORGIA'S COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM HAS 167 OFFICES, WITH PROGRAMMING IN ALL OF GEORGIA'S 159 COUNTIES. UGA PERSONNEL ARE HOUSED JOINTLY IN COUNTY OFFICES. EXTENSION DELIVERS PROGRAMMING IN AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES, FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES, AND 4-H YOUTH DEVELOPMENT AS BOTH INDIVIDUAL COUNTY EFFORTS AND AS MULTICOUNTY PROGRAMS. STATE FACULTY MEMBERS DELIVER TRAINING TO COUNTY AGENTS AND PROGRAMMING DIRECTLY TO CLIENTELE, WHEN APPROPRIATE. UGA RESEARCH PROGRAMS ARE CONDUCTED THROUGH THE AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION SYSTEM. GEORGIA HAS SEVERAL CAMPUSES THROUGHOUT THE STATE; ITS FOUR LARGEST ARE LOCATED IN ATHENS, FORT VALLEY, TIFTON AND GRIFFIN. GEORGIA HAS ELEVEN RESEARCH AND EDUCATION CENTERS STRATEGICALLY LOCATED THROUGHOUT THE STATE. THIS JOINT PLAN OF WORK WAS DEVELOPED AROUND CORE PROGRAMS AND TARGETED ISSUES. USING A STRUCTURED PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT SYSTEM, GEORGIA DEVELOPS CORE PROGRAM DIRECTIONS AND IDENTIFIES TARGETED ISSUES. THE GEORGIA PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT MODEL IS A MULTISTEP PROCESS THAT IS OPERATIONAL EVERY YEAR. THE MODEL INCLUDES A METHOD FOR ASSESSING NEEDS AND IDENTIFYING PROBLEMS. IT ALSO INCLUDES PROGRAM EVALUATION TO DETERMINE IMPACT. THE GEORGIA PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT MODEL WORKS IN UNISON WITH MULTIPLE ADVISORY SYSTEMS AT BOTH COUNTY AND STATE LEVELS. FACULTY MEMBERS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS PLAN ARE WORKING ON CUTTING-EDGE PROGRAMS. THEY PROVIDE INFORMATION AND INPUT FROM BOTH THE ACADEMIC LITERATURE AND PERSONAL KNOWLEDGE. THIS INPUT IS EQUALLY IMPORTANT TO PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT AS IS A STRONG ADVISORY SYSTEM. THE GEORGIA FEDERAL PLAN OF WORK DOES NOT ATTEMPT TO CAPTURE ALL OF THE WORK OF THE COLLEGES' FACULTY MEMBERS. IT IS INTENDED TO DOCUMENT THE PLANS AND ACTIONS OF THE FACULTY MEMBERS RECEIVING SPECIFIC FORMULA FUNDS. THE MAJORITY OF THESE FUNDS ARE USED TO SUPPORT STATE-LEVEL CORE PROGRAMS. THESE CORE PROGRAMS COVER A WIDE RANGE OF TOPICS, INCLUDING TRADITIONAL ANIMAL AND PLANT PRODUCTION, POSITIVE YOUTH AND FAMILY DEVELOPMENT, URBAN AGRICULTURE, PERSONAL HEALTH AND WELL- BEING, AND EMERGING ISSUES, SUCH AS BIOFUELS. THE GOALS OF THESE PROGRAMS ARE TO DEMONSTRATE SHORT- AND LONG-TERM IMPACT. HOWEVER, THE GREATEST IMPACTS OF THESE CORE PROGRAMS ARE THE FOUNDATIONS CREATED TO SUPPORT AND LEVERAGE ADDITIONAL RESOURCES BEYOND STATE-MATCHING FUNDS. THE ADDITIONAL STATE FUNDING, COUNTY FUNDING, GRANTS AND GIFTS LEVERAGED AS A DIRECT RESULT OF THE WORK IN THIS PLAN MAY CREATE THE GREATEST FINAL IMPACT. MOST OF GEORGIA'S PLANNED PROGRAMS INCLUDE OUTCOME MEASURES THAT TRACK THE OUTPUT LEVELS OF LEVERAGED PROGRAMMING. THE OUTPUTS OF THESE LEVERAGED PROGRAMS ARE CONSIDERED A DIRECT, SHORT-TERM OUTCOME OF THE CORE PLANNED PROGRAMS WITHIN THE GEORGIA FEDERAL PLAN OF WORK.

THE PURPOSE OF THIS FUNDING IS TO CONDUCT AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH PROGRAMS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF PUERTO RICO STATE AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION. RESEARCH EFFORTS THAT HELP TO IMPROVE THE ISLAND'S FOOD SECURITY AND THE RESILIENCY OF OUR NATURAL AND SOCIOECONOMIC SYSTEMS WERE CONSIDERED A PRIORITY. THE REGENERATION OF A SUSTAINABLE FOOD PRODUCING SECTOR IN THE CONTEXT OF A CHANGING CLIMATE AND DEMOGRAPHIC CHALLENGES IS OUR LONG-TERM GOAL. STAKEHOLDERS OF OUR PROGRAMS INCLUDE A DIVERSITY OF AUDIENCES: FARMERS, RURAL COMMUNITIES, FOOD-RELATED INDUSTRIES, SCIENTISTS AND EXTENSION SPECIALISTS, GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, ENVIRONMENTAL AND CONSERVATION CONCERNED PUBLIC, STUDENTS AND PROFESSORS, AMONG OTHERS. (2) IMPROVEMENT IN THE BIOLOGICAL EFFICIENCY OF LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION, ESTABLISHMENT OF IMPROVED FORAGES, ECONOMIC RETURNS TO PRODUCERS, AND PRACTICES THAT PROMOTE EXTREME WEATHER RESILIENCE. INITIATIVES ARE FOCUSED IN THE CHARACTERIZATION OF SLICK-HAIRED HOLSTEINS AND SENEPOL BREEDS. NEW PROJECTS ARE ALSO GEARED AT STRENGTHENING LAMB PRODUCTION AND MEAT QUALITY. (3) SUCCESSFUL ADAPTATIONS TO EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS BASED ON RISK EXPOSURE ASSESSMENTS AND AGRICULTURAL BIODIVERSITY PRACTICES; ISSUES RELATED TO SOIL QUALITY AND BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, MITIGATION OF THREATS TO WATER QUALITY, MICRO IRRIGATION TECHNOLOGIES FOR WATER CONSERVATION AND IMPROVED CROP PRODUCTIVITY, AS WELL AS THE IDENTIFICATION AND PROTECTION OF NATURAL ENEMIES OF HARMFUL INSECT PESTS; SUSTAINABLE FORESTRY; ECOSYSTEM RECOVERY; AND WETLAND ECOSYSTEMS. (4) ADDRESSING THE 2016 FDA'S FSMA REQUIREMENTS BY STAKEHOLDERS; DEVELOPMENT OF NEW PRODUCTS AND PROCESSING PROCEDURES THAT ADD VALUE TO LOCAL FARINACEOUS CROPS, FRUITS, COFFEE, AND MILK. DELIVERABLES INCLUDE PUBLICATIONS IN PEER REVIEWED JOURNALS AND POPULAR MEDIA OUTLETS (NEWSPAPERS, PODCASTS, SOCIAL MEDIA), GUIDES AND MANUALS, UPDATED TECHNOLOGICAL PACKAGES TO PRODUCE LOCAL CROPS, DETAILED PROJECT REPORTS WITH EXPERIMENTAL DATA, WORKSHOPS, FIELD DAYS AND SEMINARS, OPTIMIZATION OF PROTOCOLS FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF DIFFERENT SPECIES, POSTERS, AND ORAL PRESENTATIONS AT SCIENTIFIC AND STAKEHOLDERS' MEETINGS DEPICTING PROJECT RESULTS, AMONG OTHERS. THE TECHNOLOGY PRODUCED THROUGH THESE RESEARCH EFFORTS AND DELIVERABLES IS EXPECTED TO IMPROVE THE ISLAND'S FOOD SECURITY AND THE VIABILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY OF THE LOCAL FOOD SYSTEM. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE THE STABILIZATION OR INCREASE IN THE OUTPUT OF TARGETED COMMODITIES, THE CONSERVATION AND IMPROVEMENT OF THE SOIL AND WATER RESOURCES OF PUERTO RICO, AND THE CREATION OF NEW MARKET NICHES THAT COULD IMPACT THE EMPLOYMENT SITUATION AND WELL-BEING OF RURAL COMMUNITIES.

AUBURN UNIVERSITY IS AN 1862 LAND-GRANT INSTITUTION THAT SERVES THE CITIZENS OF ALABAMA THROUGH ITS INSTRUCTIONAL, RESEARCH, AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS. AAES OPERATIONS ARE SUPPORTED WITH FUNDING FROM THE USDA NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURE (NIFA) HATCH PROGRAM AND THE STATE OF ALABAMA. ALL PLANNED PROGRAMS ARE DEVELOPED WITHIN THE CONTEXT OF RESEARCH AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT WITHRELEVANCE TO ALL RESIDENTS OF ALABAMA WHO MAY BENEFIT FROM THE LOCAL KNOWLEDGE BASE OR SERVICE. WE ARE COGNIZANT OF THE NECESSITY TO CONTINUE TO ADDRESS NIFA PRIORITIES, WHICH ARE PRIORITIES FOR ALABAMA RESIDENTS AS WELL. THE PURPOSE OF THIS FUNDING IS TO CONDUCT AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH PROGRAMS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF PUERTO RICO STATE AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION. HATCH SUPPORTED ACTIVITIES INCLUDE RESEARCH ON:  O STRATEGIES TO INCREASE CROP PRODUCTION, POST-HARVEST CROP MANAGEMENT AND IMPROVE MARKETING EFFICIENCY; EVALUATION OF DISEASE RESISTANT CROP VARIETIES AND PRACTICES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF VECTORS; INTRODUCTION OF NEW GERMPLASM ADDRESSING PRODUCTION CONSTRAINTS OR PROMISING NEW CROPS; EVALUATION OF PRODUCTION UNDER PROTECTED STRUCTURES; CONTINUED SURVEILLANCE OF OUR CURRENT CROPS AND FARMING SYSTEMS, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TO CONTROL THE MAJOR PESTS AND DISEASES AFFECTING OUR MOST IMPORTANT CROPS.  O IMPROVEMENT IN THE BIOLOGICAL EFFICIENCY OF LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION, ESTABLISHMENT OF IMPROVED FORAGES, ECONOMIC RETURNS TO THE PRODUCERS, AND PRACTICES THAT PROMOTE EXTREME WEATHER RESILIENCE. INITIATIVES ARE FOCUSED ON THE CHARACTERIZATION OF SLICK-HAIRED HOLSTEINS AND SENEPOL BREEDS. NEW PROJECTS ARE ALSO GEARED TOWARDS STRENGTHENING LAMB PRODUCTION AND MEAT QUALITY.  O SUCCESSFUL ADAPTATION TO EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS BASED ON RISK EXPOSURE ASSESSMENTS AND AGRICULTURAL BIODIVERSITY PRACTICES; ISSUES RELATED TO SOIL QUALITY AND BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, MITIGATION OF THREATS TO WATER QUALITY, MICRO IRRIGATION TECHNOLOGIES FOR WATER CONSERVATION AND IMPROVED CROP PRODUCTIVITY, AS WELL AS THE IDENTIFICATION AND PROTECTION OF THE NATURAL ENEMIES OF HARMFUL INSECT PESTS; SUSTAINABLE FORESTRY; ECOSYSTEM RECOVERY; AND WETLAND ECOSYSTEMS. THE PURPOSE OF THIS AWARD IS TO SUPPORT MULTISTATE RESEARCH PROJECTS CONDUCTED BY FACULTY ACROSS THE COLLEGE THAT HELP ADDRESS THE CRITICAL ISSUES IDENTIFIED IN THE FY2023 KENTUCKY PLAN OF WORK: AGRICULTURAL, ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES, ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL WELL-BEING, FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY, AND NUTRITION AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES. PROJECTS REPRESENT BOTH BASIC AND APPLIED SCIENCES AND MANY RESEARCH PROJECTS ARE INTEGRATED WITH EXTENSION PROGRAMS THAT HELP DELIVER SOLUTIONS TO OUR STAKEHOLDERS IN THE STATE, REGION, AND NATION. MULTISTATE RESEARCH IN SUPPORT OF AGRICULTURAL, ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES WILL ADDRESS A WIDE ARRAY OF ISSUES RELATED TO PLANT AND ANIMAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS AND THE PROTECTION OF NATURAL RESOURCES. RESEARCH PROJECTS WILL ALSO ADDRESS THE OVERALL SUSTAINABILITY OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AS IT CONTRIBUTES TO FOOD AVAILABILITY AND THE STABILITY AND EXPANSION OF AGRICULTURAL MARKETS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED CROPPING, HORTICULTURAL, AND ANIMAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS THAT IMPROVE PRODUCTION EFFICIENCIES WHILE REDUCING NEGATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS, NEW UNDERSTANDING AND TREATMENTS FOR PROTECTING PLANTS AND ANIMALS FROM PESTS AND DISEASES, THE CREATION AND ADOPTION OF CLIMATE-SMART PRACTICES FOR KENTUCKY PRODUCERS, EXPANDED ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES FOR AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISES THROUGH THE CREATION OF NEW PRODUCTS AND MARKET OPPORTUNITIES. MULTISTATE RESEARCH IN SUPPORT OF ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL WELL-BEING WILL INVESTIGATE THE WILLINGNESS OF CONSUMERS TO SUPPORT MINORITY AND DISADVANTAGED FARMER BUSINESSES AND EXPLORE THE CHALLENGES FACED BY FAMILY FARMS IN BALANCING GROWN OF THE FARM ENTERPRISE WITH THEIR HOUSEHOLD GOALS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF THIS WORK INCLUDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF CONSUMER MOTIVATIONS AND RESOURCES NEEDED TO SUPPORT THE GROWTH AND SUSTAINABILITY OF SMALL TO MID-SIZED FARMING OPERATIONS. FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY MULTISTATE PROJECTS INVESTIGATE FACTORS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO FOOD SAFETY VULNERABILITIES AND SEEK TO BETTER UNDERSTAND WAYS IN WHICH THREATS CAN BE CONTROLLED PRE- AND POST- HARVEST. RESEARCH ALSO INVESTIGATES HOW FOOD SAFETY INCIDENTS AND POLICIES IMPACT SUPPLY CHAINS AND CONSUMER PRICES AND BEHAVIOR. OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE BETTER METHODS FOR DETECTING AND PREVENTING HEALTH RISKS IN FOODS AS WELL AS IMPROVED MARKET RESILIENCY AGAINST DISRUPTIONS CAUSE BY CONTAMINATION EVENTS. MULTISTATE RESEARCH RELATED TO NUTRITION AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLE IS STUDYING HOW NUTRITION INTERVENTIONS CAN BE COMBINED WITH ONLINE S HOPPING TO INFLUENCE HEALTHY SHOPPING PATTERNS. THE WORK IS EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE TO IMPROVED HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR SOME OF THE STATE'S MOST VULNERABLE POPULATIONS. MULTISTATE RESEARCH ALSO IS WORKING TO UNDERSTAND TICK DISTRIBUTIONS AND SEASONAL ACTIVITY, AS WELL AS DEVELOPING TARGETED NON-TOXIC CONTROL METHODS FOR MOSQUITOS. OUTCOMES OF PUBLIC HEALTH ENTOMOLOGY RESEARCH WILL BE IMPROVED VECTOR-BORNE DISEASE PREVENTION EFFORTS. DELIVERABLES FROM THE RESEARCH PROGRAMS SUPPORTEDBY HATCH MULTISTATE FUNDING INCLUDE NEW DATA, SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS AND PRESENTATIONS, TECHNOLOGIES, PLANT VARIETIES AND THE NEXT GENERATION OF SCIENTISTS TRAINED THROUGH PARTICIPATION IN PROJECTS. TRANSLATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS TO STAKEHOLDERS WILL BE THROUGH NEW DECISIONS SUPPORT TOOLS, LAY PUBLICATIONS AND EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING DEVELOPED AND DELIVERED IN COLLABORATION WITH EXTENSION. RESEARCH IN SUPPORT OF AGRICULTURAL, ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES WILL ADDRESS A WIDE ARRAY OF ISSUES RELATED TO PLANT AND ANIMAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS AND THE PROTECTION OF NATURAL RESOURCES. RESEARCH PROJECTS WILL ALSO ADDRESS THE OVERALL SUSTAINABILITY OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AS IT CONTRIBUTES TO FOOD AVAILABILITY AND THE STABILITY AND EXPANSION OF AGRICULTURAL MARKETS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED CROPPING, HORTICULTURAL, AND ANIMAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS THAT IMPROVE PRODUCTION EFFICIENCIES WHILE REDUCING NEGATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS, NEW UNDERSTANDING AND TREATMENTS FOR PROTECTING PLANTS AND ANIMALS FROM PESTS AND DISEASES, THE CREATION AND ADOPTION OF CLIMATE-SMART PRACTICES FOR KENTUCKY PRODUCERS, EXPANDED ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES FOR AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISES THROUGH THE CREATION OF NEW PRODUCTS AND MARKET OPPORTUNITIES. RESEARCH IN SUPPORT OF ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL WELL-BEING WILL ADDRESS ISSUES RELATED TO AGRICULTURAL PRODUCT VALUE AND SUPPLY CHAINS AND THEIR IMPACT ON SUSTAINABILITY, CONSUMER ACCESS AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES FOR PRODUCERS. RESEARCH ALSO HELPS INFORM PRODUCER DECISION MAKING FOR ON-FARM PROFITABILITY. RURAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IS ALSO A FOCUS OF RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO THIS CRITICAL ISSUE. EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF THIS WORK INCLUDE HIGHER PROFIT MARGINS AND EXPANDED ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES AND MARKETS FOR PRODUCERS. RURAL COMMUNITIES ARE ALSO EXPECTED TO BENEFIT FROM BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF FACTORS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND COMMUNITY VITALITY.  FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY PROJECTS CONSIDER BIOLOGICAL AND CHEMICAL ATTRIBUTES THAT CONTRIBUTE TO SAFETY VULNERABILITIES AND PROTECTION IN FOOD PRODUCTION AND PROCESSING, AS WELL AS HOW FOOD SAFETY INCIDENTS AND POLICIES IMPACT SUPPLY CHAINS AND CONSUMER PRICES AND BEHAVIOR. OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE BETTER METHODS FOR DETECTING AND PREVENTING HEALTH RISKS IN FOODS AS WELL AS IMPROVED MARKET RESILIENCY AGAINST DISRUPTIONS CAUSE BY CONTAMINATION EVENTS.  RESEARCH CONTRIBUTING TO LIFE SKILLS DEVELOPMENT STRIVES TO UNDERSTAND HOW AGRICULTURAL EDUCATORS CAN BE EFFECTIVE IN WORKING WITH CULTURALLY DIVERSE CLIENTELE. THIS WORK WILL EXPAND AGRICULTURAL LITERACY, IMPROVE ACCEPTANCE OF MODERN AGRICULTURAL SCIENCE AND ENTREPRENEURIAL THINKING AMONG UNDERSERVED YOUTH.  NUTRITION AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLE RESEARCH PROJECTS STRIVE TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW NUTRITION CAN MITIGATE HEALTH RISKS FROM ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES AND DEVELOP EFFECTIVE NUTRITION HEALTH INTERVENTIONS FOR DIVERSE POPULATIONS. THE WORK IS EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE TO IMPROVED HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR SOME OF THE STATE'S MOST VULNERABLE POPULATIONS. RESEARCH IN PUBLIC HEALTH ENTOMOLOGY ALSO CONTRIBUTES TO HEALTHY LIFESTYLES BY SEEKING WAYS TO CONTROL INSECT DISEASE VECTORS.  DELIVERABLES FROM THE RESEARCH PROGRAMS SUPPORTED BY HATCH FUNDING INCLUDE NEW DATA, SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS AND PRESENTATIONS, TECH NOLOGIES, PLANT VARIETIES AND THE NEXT GENERATION OF SCIENTISTS TRAINED THROUGH PARTICIPATION IN PROJECTS. TRANSLATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS TO STAKEHOLDERS WILL BE THROUGH NEW DECISIONS SUPPORT TOOLS, LAY PUBLICATIONS AND EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING DEVELOPED AND DELIVERED IN COLLABORATION WITH EXTENSION. BENEFICIARIES WILL INCLUDE OTHER SCIENTISTS, AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS, AGRIBUSINESSES, RURAL COMMUNITIES, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
FISCAL YEAR 2022-THE HATCH ACT OF 1887 (MULTISTATE RESEARCH FUND)

AS THE ONLY RESEARCH UNIVERSITY IN THE STATE, AND AS A LAND-GRANT INSTITUTION, WE ARE CHARGED WITH INTEGRATING HIGHER EDUCATION, RESEARCH, AND EXTENSION TO MEET THE NEEDS OF VERMONT CITIZENS, COMMUNITIES, AND ORGANIZATIONS. WE ACCOMPLISH THIS IN PART WITH RESEARCH CONDUCTED THROUGH THE VERMONT AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (AES) THAT FOCUSES ON CONTEMPORARY PROBLEMS, NEEDS, AND CHALLENGES OF A CHANGING STATE AND WORLD. OUR EFFORTS SUPPORT INDUSTRIES ASSOCIATED WITH THE WORKING LANDSCAPE, FROM FOOD SYSTEMS SUPPLY CHAINS TO THE RECREATION ECONOMY, INCLUDING CONSERVATION, PRESERVATION, AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES. WE HAVE THEREFORE IDENTIFIED SIX AREAS WITHIN WHICH WE CONDUCT OUR TRANSDISCIPLINARY WORK:  O ANIMAL HEALTH, PRODUCTION, AND PRODUCTS O DEVELOPMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY OF COMMUNITIES O FOUNDATIONAL AND EXPLORATORY RESEARCH IN AGRICULTURE O NUTRITIONAL VALUE, FOOD SECURITY, AND FOOD SAFETY O QUALITY OF THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENT O SUSTAINABILITY OF VERMONT AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND FORESTS  AES ADDRESSES THESE CRITICAL ISSUES FACING VERMONT BY CONDUCTING RESEARCH AND DISSEMINATING ESSENTIAL CURRENT SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION TO A BROAD RANGE OF AUDIENCES. THIS INCREASES THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS AND ENCOURAGES IMPLEMENTATION OF COST-EFFECTIVE, ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES.

positiveFlows.title: THE PURPOSE OF THESE FUNDS IS TO CONDUCT RESEARCH IN ALL ASPECTS OF AGRICULTURE, INCLUDING PLANT AND  ANIMAL HEALTH, PRODUCTION AND PROTECTION, SOIL AND WATER CONSERVATION, AGRICULTURAL ECONOMICS, NUTRITION,  SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND OTHER EMERGING AGRICULTURAL PROBLEMS AT THE LOCAL, STATE, NATIONAL AND  WORLDWIDE LEVEL.  AGRILIFE RESEARCH STRIVES TO CREATE, LEARN, AND SHARE KNOWLEDGE ABOUT AGRICULTURE AND THE LIFE SCIENCES  THAT NOURISHES HEALTH, PROTECTS NATURAL RESOURCES, AND SUPPORTS AGRICULTURAL ECONOMIES. OUR RESEARCH  ENSURES HEALTHY LIVES AND LIVELIHOODS IMPROVE THROUGH ABUNDANT, AFFORDABLE, AND HIGH-QUALITY FOOD AND  AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS IN TEXAS AND THE WORLD. AGRILIFE RESEARCH IS COMMITTED TO DELIVERING CUTTING-EDGE  SCIENTIFIC TOOLS AND INNOVATIVE SOLUTIONS FOR TEXAS PRODUCERS, INDUSTRY MEMBERS, AND URBAN AND RURAL  COMMUNITIES TO SUPPORT THE NOURISHMENT AND WELL-BEING OF ALL PEOPLE. THESE EFFORTS LEAD TO THE STABILITY  AND CONTINUAL ENHANCEMENT OF OUR STATE'S AGROECOSYSTEMS AND NATURAL RESOURCES, FURTHER ENSURING THE  ECONOMIC COMPETITIVENESS AND EXCELLENCE OF AGRICULTURE AND HUMAN HEALTH.  RECENT HATCH-SUPPORTED RESEARCH AT TEXAS A<(>&<)>M AGRILIFE RESEARCH HAS LED TO ADVANCES IN AGRICULTURAL  PRODUCTIVITY AND ECONOMIC IMPACT. NOTABLE OUTCOMES INCLUDE THE DEVELOPMENT OF DROUGHT- AND DISEASE RESISTANT CROP VARIETIES, IMPROVED MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT ENHANCE SOIL HEALTH AND WATER USE  EFFICIENCY, AND NEW TECHNOLOGIES FOR PEST AND DISEASE CONTROL. THESE EFFORTS HAVE RESULTED IN INCREASED  YIELDS, REDUCED INPUT COSTS, AND MORE RESILIENT CROPPING SYSTEMS FOR TEXAS PRODUCERS. RESEARCH ON FOOD  SAFETY, ANIMAL HEALTH, AND LIVESTOCK MANAGEMENT HAS ALSO CONTRIBUTED TO IMPROVED PUBLIC HEALTH AND  GREATER PROFITABILITY FOR AGRICULTURAL STAKEHOLDERS. COLLECTIVELY, THESE IMPACTS SUPPORT THE CONTINUED  VITALITY OF TEXAS AGRICULTURE AND BENEFIT PRODUCERS, CONSUMERS, AND RURAL COMMUNITIES STATEWIDE.  AGRILIFE RESEARCH IS WORKING TO FIND INNOVATIVE SOLUTIONS THAT WILL CREATE ADAPTIVE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS -  SYSTEMS THAT CAN MEET THE DEMAND OF A GROWING POPULATION, RESILIENCE TO WEATHER EXTREMES, FLUCTUATING  ECONOMIC CONDITIONS, UNPREDICTABLE GEOPOLITICAL ENVIRONMENTS, DECLINING RESOURCES, AND PUBLIC HEALTH  CRISES. OUR STRATEGIC RESEARCH PLAN AIMS AT MAKING FUNDAMENTAL SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERIES AND APPLYING THEM  TO CREATE NEW TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL ENHANCE THE SUSTAINABILITY AND RESILIENCE OF ADAPTIVE AGRICULTURAL  SYSTEMS. THESE AGILE SYSTEMS CAN MEET THE NEEDS NOT ONLY OF FOOD AND FIBER, BUT ALSO OF CLEAN WATER AND  AIR, FUNCTIONAL LANDSCAPES, IMPROVED HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, AND THE SUSTAINABILITY OF RESOURCES FOR  GENERATIONS TO COME. THE FOLLOWING ARE FOUR BROAD PRIORITY AREAS THAT AGRILIFE RESEARCH FOCUSES ON:  1. DISCOVER NEW INNOVATIONS, TECHNOLOGIES, AND SCIENCE-BASED SOLUTIONS TO ENHANCE AGRICULTURAL  AND ECOLOGICAL SYSTEMS, AND THE LIFE SCIENCES.  2. PROVIDE THE TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH NECESSARY TO DEVELOP AND PRODUCE HIGH-QUALITY, SAFE, AND  SUSTAINABLE FOOD AND FIBER SYSTEMS WITH LOCAL, NATIONAL, AND GLOBAL IMPACTS.  3. ENHANCE THE EFFICIENCY, PROFITABILITY, AND RESILIENCY OF AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND  FOOD SYSTEMS IN THE STATE OF TEXAS AND THE WORLD.  4. DISCOVER, DISSEMINATE, AND FACILITATE THE ADOPTION OF SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE AT THE INTERSECTION  OF NUTRITION, HUMAN HEALTH, AND AGRICULTURE.  AGRILIFE RESEARCH ALLOCATES THESE HATCH FUNDS THROUGHOUT THE AGENCY FOR THE RESEARCHERS TO CONDUCT  THEIR RESEARCH AND GROW THEIR PROGRAMS. RESEARCHERS ARE EXPECTED TO PUBLISH THEIR RESULTS AND GROW  THEIR RESEARCH PROGRAM THROUGH OTHER EXTERNAL SPONSORED RESEARCH PROJECTS. THE CITIZENS OF TEXAS, THE  US AND THE WORLD BENEFIT FROM THE RESEARCH DONE BY THESE RESEARCHERS.

THROUGH INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS, NC STATE IS SOLVING CHALLENGES RELATED TO THE PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY OF BOTH LARGE- AND SMALL-SCALE FARMS. RESEARCHERS AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS ARE ALSO DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE LANDSCAPING AND GARDENING. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS ARE FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND METHODS FOR ANIMAL BREEDING, REPRODUCTION, NUTRITION, GENETICS AND GENOMICS, PHYSIOLOGY, ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS, PRODUCT QUALITY, AND HEALTH AND WELL-BEING. THESE INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS ALSO AIM TO TACKLE THE CRITICAL ISSUES IMPACTING THE QUALITY OF OUR SOIL, WATER AND AIR BY PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC SOLUTIONS FOR ANIMAL WASTE MANAGEMENT, WASTEWATER TREATMENT, NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT, SEPTIC SYSTEMS, WETLAND MANAGEMENT, SOIL PROPERTIES, AND FISHERY AND POND MANAGEMENT. NC STATE'S RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS TO ENHANCE FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH AND TO KEEP AMERICAN'S HEALTHY AND FREE FROM FOODBORNE ILLNESS NECESSITATE A FOCUS ON PREVENTING FOOD SAFETY PROBLEMS RATHER THAN TAKING A REACTIONARY APPROACH. NC STATE'S INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS FOCUS ON PROTECTING THE SAFETY OF FOODS ALONG THE ENTIRE SUPPLY CHAIN, FROM PRODUCTION TO CONSUMPTION. TO MEET THE GROWING  NEED FOR HEALTHY FOOD, RESEARCHERS ARE DEVELOPING AND PRODUCING NEW FOOD PRODUCTS THAT PROMOTE HEALTH AND PREVENT DISEASE. AT THE SAME TIME, EXTENSION PROVIDES NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMMING TO ENSURE THAT INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE THEY NEED TO MAKE INFORMED CHOICES ABOUT FOOD AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES. IMPROVING PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS: WITHIN THIS AREA, WE WILL WORK TO ADDRESS CROSSCUTTING AND EMERGING ISSUES OF ANIMAL AND PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION. IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY THE EFFICIENCY OF DIFFERENT FEEDING SOURCES TO IMPROVE ANIMAL PRODUCTIVITY AND GUT HEALTH. IN PLANT SYSTEMS, THE FOCUS WILL BE ON PRACTICAL APPROACHES SUCH AS CROP PRODUCTION, SEASON EXTENSION, ADAPTATION TO CHANGING AGRICULTURAL CONDITIONS, VALUE-ADDED AGRICULTURE, DIGITAL TOOLS, SOIL HEALTH, PEST CONTROL, AND FARM ECONOMICS. EXTENSION WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND ITSWORK WITH LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS, PLACING SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON LIMITED RESOURCES, SMALL- SCALE FARMERS.THE FARM PAVILION WILL FOCUS ON SUSTAINABLE AG RICULTURE AND LOCAL ANDCOMMUNITY FOOD SYSTEMS, HOUSING ITS APPLIED RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION PROGRAMS' STAFF AND PROVIDING SPACE FOR MEETINGS, FORUMS AND CONFERENCES.

THE OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY APPROVED PLAN OF WORK (POW) ENCOMPASSES A FIVE-YEAR PERIOD AND REPRESENTS A JOINT EFFORT BY THE TWO CRITICAL COMPONENTS OF OSU'S COLLEGE OF FOOD, AGRICULTURAL, AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES (CFAES), THE OHIO AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (OARDC) AND OSU EXTENSION. CFAES RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS ARE CONDUCTED IN NINE ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS ON OUR CAMPUSES IN COLUMBUS AND WOOSTER, ELEVEN RESEARCH STATIONS AND FIELD LABS, AND IN ALL 88 COUNTIES THROUGHOUT THE STATE. WHILE THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY IS THE LARGEST INDUSTRY IN THE BUCKEYE STATE, CFAES RESEARCH REACHES BEYOND AGRICULTURE AND COVERS ENVIRONMENTAL, WATER QUALITY AND SOCIETAL ISSUES THAT RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES FACE. THE CFAES STRATEGIC PLAN INCLUDES: GOAL 1 STUDENT/LEARNER FIRST PHILOSOPHY, CFAES TEACHING REACHES ACROSS THE LIFESPAN FROM YOUTH SERVED THROUGH 4-H PROGRAMS TO STUDENTS PURSUING DEGREES ON CAMPUS TO 2 MILLION PLUS LIFELONG LEARNERS IN EXTENSION PROGRAMS. GOAL 2 INNOVATIVE SCHOLARSHIP TO SUSTAIN LIFE, CFAES RESEARCH PROJECTS AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS ADDRESS OUR CRITICAL ISSUES WHICH COVER AREAS IN HEALTH AND WELLNESS, ECONOMIC VITALITY, FOOD SECURITY AND PRODUCTION, ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY AS WELL AS HELPING PEOPLE THRIVE ACROSS THE LIFESPAN. GOAL 3 CAPACITY BUILDING OF OUR PEOPLE AND OUR COMMUNITIES. PEOPLE ARE OUR GREATEST ASSET AND CFAES STRIVES TO BUILD ON THE SUCCESS OF OUR PEOPLE. CHANGING WORKFORCE DYNAMICS, MARKET COMPETITION, ECONOMIC DRIVERS, AN INCREASING DESIRE FOR A MORE BALANCED APPROACH TO HOW LIFE AND WORK INTERFACE, AND A NEED FOR DIVERSIFYING OUR TALENT. GOAL 4 PARTNER OF CHOICE, CFAES WANTS TO ENGAGE OUR ENTIRE COMMUNITY, INCLUDING BOTH INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL STAKEHOLDERS. GOAL 5 RESOURCE STEWARDSHIP IN A ONE-COLLEGE MODEL, CFAES CONTINUES TO TRANSFORM AND IMPROVE OUR PHYSICAL ENVIRONMENT ACROSS OUR THREE CAMPUSES. RECENTLY COMPLETED PROJECTS INCLUDE A NEW SCIENCE BUILDING PROVIDING MODERN RESEARCH SPACE ON THE WOOSTER CAMPUS AND THE NEW CONTROLLED ENVIRONMENT AGRICULTURE RESEARCH COMPLEX AT WATERMAN FARM ON THE COLUMBUS CAMPUS. THE MULTISPECIES ANIMAL LEARNING CENTER IS UNDER CONSTRUCTION AT THE WATERMAN FARM ON THE COLUMBUS CAMPUS. THE JOINT POW WAS DEVELOPED AROUND THESE GOALS AS WELL AS FIVE CRITICAL ISSUES. 1 HEALTH AND WELLNESS, EXPLORING HEALTH RELATED ISSUES INCLUDING CHRONIC DISEASE PREVENTION, OBESITY REDUCTION, COMMUNITY NUTRITION EDUCATION, FARM SAFETY, AND PRACTICAL APPROACHES TO IMPROVING OVERALL WELL-BEING FOR INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES. 2 ECONOMIC VITALITY, ISSUES RELATED TO ECONOMIC VITALITY INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO BUSINESS RETENTION AND EXPANSION, ENHANCING RURAL ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES, INCREASING BROADBAND ACCESS IN RURAL AREAS, THE EFFECTS OF TRADE POLICIES ON FOOD AND AG INDUSTRIES, AND THE ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF ECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT. 3 FOOD SECURITY AND PRODUCTION, WE WILL EXPLORE ISSUES RELATED TO MITIGATING FOOD INSECURITY THROUGH COMMUNITY SERVICE AND FOOD PRODUCTION EDUCATION PROGRAMS AND FOOD SYSTEM ENHANCEMENTS INCLUDING DIGITAL AGRICULTURE, RESILIENCE TO EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS, IMPROVED FOOD ANIMAL HEALTH AND PRODUCTION, CROP IMPROVEMENT, WEED AND PEST CONTROL, PLANT BREEDING AND DISEASE RESISTANCE, NUTRIENT DENSE FOODS, NEW FOOD PRESERVATIVES, AND ANTIMICROBIAL FOOD PACKAGING. 4 ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY AND PRODUCTION EFFICIENCY. RESEARCH TOPICS COVER AREAS SUCH AS SOIL HEALTH AND REMEDIATION, BIOLOGICAL CONTROL AGENTS, REDUCTION OF PESTICIDE USE, PRODUCTION OF POLYMERS AND BIOPLASTICS, WATER QUALITY AND WASTEWATER TREATMENT, AQUATIC ECOSYSTEM HEALTH, AIR QUALITY AND PRODUCTION OF BIOPRODUCTS AND RENEWABLE FUELS. 5 THRIVING ACROSS THE LIFESPAN, PROGRAMS UNDER THIS CRITICAL ISSUE ARE RELATED TO POSITIVE HUMAN DEVELOPMENT FOR ALL AGES. A MAJOR FOCUS IS YOUTH DEVELOPMENT THROUGH 4-H AND FINANCIAL LITERACY PROGRAMS. THE CFAES GOALS AND WORK ON THE CRITICAL ISSUES DIRECTLY AND INDIRECTLY BENEFIT FARMERS, RANCHERS AND FORESTERS ACROSS OHIO AND BEYOND.

THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES AT PENN STATE WILL PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE SUPPORT TO THE RESIDENTS OF PENNSYLVANIA THROUGH THE A CTIVITIES OF THE PENNSYLVANIA AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (AES) AND PENN STATE EXTENSION (EXTENSION). WE WILL BE RESPONSIVE TO STAKEHOLDER NEEDS THROUGH TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH AND DELIVERY OF SCIENCE-BASED PROGRAMS TO CLIENTELE, BUT WE WILL ALSO CONDUCT REGION ALLY, NATIONALLY, AND INTERNATIONALLY RELEVANT FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH THAT GENERATES BASELINE DATA TO SOLVE FUTURE NEEDS RELATIVE TO AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND ACTIVELY SEEK NEW AND BETTER WAYS TO COMMUNICATE OUR PROGRAMS TO NEW AUDIENCES. OUR FACULTY AND STAFF, SUPPORTED BY FEDERAL BASE FUNDING (TO INCLUDE HATCH AND MULTISTATE HATCH FUNDS), WILL EFFECTIVELY LEVERAGE THIS INVESTMENT AGAINST MANY OTHER EXTERNAL FUNDING SOURCES TO CONDUCT PROGRAMS OF THE HIGHEST CALIBER. WE ARE COMMITTED TO EXCELLENCE IN RESEARCH, EDUCATING THE NEXT GENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS AND CITIZENS, AND PROMOTING LIFE-LONG LEARNING AMONG THE CITIZENS OF PENNSYLVANIA AND WITHIN THE REGION AND NATION. OUR MISSION IS CLEAR: 'THE MISSION OF THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES IS TO DISCOVER, INTEGRATE, TRANSLATE, AND DISSEMINATE KNOWLEDGE TO ENHANCE THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SYSTEM, NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP, AND ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL WELLBEING, THEREBY IMPROVING THE LIVES OF PEOPLE IN PENNSYLVANIA, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD.' AGRICULTURE FACES CHALLENGES OF RISING ENERGY COSTS, WEATHER EXTREMES, AN EXPANDING HUMAN POPULATION, ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION, LOSS OF BIODIVERSITY, LABOR SHORTAGES, ARMED CONFLICT, AND A LINGERING PANDEMIC. TO HELP MEET THESE CHALLENGES, WE ARE DEVELOPING A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK BASED ON THE SCIENCE OF AGRICULTURAL SUSTAINABILITY, DEFINED AS THE INTEGRATION OF NATURAL AND SOCIAL SCIENCES TO INFORM PRACTICE AND POLICY FOR PRODUCTIVE, WORKING LANDSCAPES, HEALTHY WATERSHEDS, AND RESILIENT ECONOMIES. THIS INNOVATIVE APPROACH TO AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH, ENGAGEMENT, AND EDUCATION CENTERS ON THE IMPACTS AND SYNERGIES OF CONTIGUOUS RURAL AND URBAN LANDSCAPES. THIS MOSAIC OF DENSELY POPULATED AREAS NEXT TO FORESTS AND AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES IS UNIQUE TO PENNSYLVANIA AND THE MID-ATLANTIC REGION AND REQUIRES AN INTEGRATED STRATEGY TO ACHIEVE HEALTHY AND THRIVING AGRICULTURE, NATURAL SYSTEMS, ECONOMIES, AND COMMUNITIES. A PRIMARY COMPONENT OF AES AND EXTENSION WORK IN OUR COLLEGE WILL BE BUILT ON THE THREE INTEGRATED PILLARS OF INTENSIFICATION, RESILIENCE, AND REGENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES AS SOLUTIONS TO SOME OF THE MOST VEXING PROBLEMS CONFRONTING PENNSYLVANIA AND SIMILAR MOSAIC LANDSCAPES WORLDWIDE. WE WILL HOLISTICALLY AND COMPREHENSIVELY ADDRESS THESE CRITICAL ISSUES: INCREASING THE EFFICIENCY AND PROFITABILITY OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION WHILE MINIMIZING ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS AND IMPROVE HUMAN HEALTH, EQUIPPING FARMERS TO ABSORB AND RECOVER FROM SHORT-TERM EMERGENCIES AND LONG-TERM STRESSES TO THEIR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND LIVELIHOODS, OPTIMIZING PLANTS, ANIMALS, AND ECOSYSTEMS FOR RESILIENCE TO AND FASTER RECOVERY FROM ENVIRONMENTALLY RELATED STRESSES, DEVELOPING STRATEGIES FOR BETTER MANAGEMENT OF NUTRIENT INPUTS AND OUTPUTS ACROSS COMPLEX AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL RESOURCE SYSTEMS, FROM LOCAL FIELDS AND FARMS TO LARGE WATERSHEDS, HARNESSING SPATIAL DATA AND REMOTE SENSING TECHNOLOGIES TO MAP AND MODEL PREDICTIVE SIMULATIONS OF ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE.

DESCRIPTION OF AWARD AND ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: THE ACES OFFICE OF RESEARCH AND AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION ENABLES AND ENCOURAGES FACULTY CREATIVITY AND INTERDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATION TO ADVANCE THE MISSION OF THE COLLEGE AND THE BROADER MISSION OF OUR LAND GRANT UNIVERSITY. WE ACCOMPLISH THIS THROUGH CAPACITY FUND INVESTMENTS IN SEED FUNDING, EQUIPMENT, RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE, TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES, AND STRATEGIC INITIATIVES. DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES: ACTIVITIES FOCUS ON FIVE CRITICAL ISSUES. 1. COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT, LEADERSHIP, AND VITALITY- WE STUDY: RURAL POPULATION CHANGE AND ADAPTATION IN THE FACE OF HEALTH AND ECONOMIC SHOCK AND STRESSORS, RURAL YOUTH RISK-TAKING DECISION-MAKING TO TRANSFORM THE DEVELOPMENTAL TRAJECTORY FROM VULNERABILITY TO RESILIENCY, AND THE INFLUENCE OF CONNECTEDNESS AND INTERPERSONAL RELATIONSHIPS IN ADOLESCENTS. 2. ECONOMIC AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT- WE STUDY: AGRICULTURAL AND RURAL MARKETS, INCLUDING ACCESS, PRICING AND TRADING DYNAMICS AND LEGAL AND POLICY ISSUES; THE ECONOMIC INCENTIVES FOR ADOPTING NEW AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGIES, CROPS, AND PRACTICES AND THEIR IMPLICATIONS FOR LAND USE, FARM PROFITABILITY, CONSUMER AND PRODUCERS AND THE ENVIRONMENT; CREATING RESILIENT ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT FOR RURAL POPULATIONS. 3. SAFE, HEALTHY ENVIRONMENTS AND BEHAVIORS- WE STUDY: NUTRITION, INCLUDING HOW AGING DISRUPTS THE BODY'S ABILITY TO ABSORB LIPIDS, AND A STUDY OF THE ROLE OF THE INTESTINAL MICROBIOME IN PERSONALIZED METABOLIC RESPONSES TO DIET; THE SOCIAL ENVIRONMENT'S IMPACT ON WELLNESS, INCLUDING HOW ECONOMIC UNCERTAINTY AND EXPOSURE TO CRIME INFLUENCE CHILD DEVELOPMENT; CANCER AND DISEASES, INCLUDING THE ROLE OF THERMALLY ABUSED FRYING OIL ON LATE-STAGE CANCER PROGRESSION, PRENATAL GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT DURING MATERNAL INFLUENZA INFECTION AND THE USE OF NEW TYPES OF MEDICAL IMAGING TO DETECT ATHEROSCLEROTIC CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. 4. EFFECTIVE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND FOOD SYSTEMS- WE STUDY: FIELD CROP IMPROVEMENT, INCLUDING PHENOTYPIC SELECTION, MOLECULAR BREEDING AND GENOME EDITING; PLANT PROTECTION, WITH ACTIVITIES CENTERED ON WEED MANAGEMENT, PLANT PATHOLOGY, AND ENTOMOLOGY; THE ACCURATE REPRESENTATION AND MEASUREMENT OF AGRONOMIC AND HORTICULTURAL CROPPING SYSTEMS UNDER FIELD CONDITIONS; NEXT-GENERATION APPROACHES TO CROP RESEARCH EMPLOYING REMOTELY-SENSED FIELD DATA, MINING GLOBAL DATA SETS, AND DEVELOPING ADVANCED GENOMIC PREDICTION MODELS; AND ANIMAL AND VETERINARY RESEARCH TO IMPROVE THE EFFICIENCY, SAFETY AND SECURITY OF ANIMAL PRODUCTION; AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW FOOD PRODUCTS. 5. THRIVING NATURAL RESOURCES- WE STUDY: THE RESPONSE OF SOIL AND WATER QUALITY TO MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT OF TERRESTRIAL AND AQUATIC ANIMALS, AND ECO SYSTEMS AND THEIR ABILITY TO PROVISION SERVICES UNDER DEVELOPMENT AND MANAGEMENT CONDITIONS. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: WE SEEK INPUT FROM DIVERSE GROUPS AND INDIVIDUALS TO ENSURE OUR PROGRAMS REMAIN SOCIALLY RELEVANT. THESE GROUPS INCLUDE STUDENTS (THE NEXT GENERATION OF PROFESSIONALS, SCIENTISTS AND EDUCATORS), FELLOW RESEARCHERS AND EXTENSION SPECIALISTS, GROWERS, COMMODITY GROUPS, COMMUNITY O RGANIZATIONS, LAWMAKERS, AND INDUSTRY REPRESENTATIVES. WE IDENTIFY STAKEHOLDERS IN ILLINOIS FOCUSING ON LOCAL ISSUES, AND BEYOND THE STATE FOCUSING ON ISSUES OF REGIONAL OR NATIONAL CONCERN. WE DO NOT EXPECT ANY SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES.

HATCH CAPACITY GRANT FUNDS ARE USED TO CONDUCT RESEARCH ACROSS DISCIPLINES IN AGRICULTURE, FOOD, ANIMAL AND HUMAN HEALTH TO ADVANCE PRODUCTION AND PROVIDE AN ADEQUATE AND NUTRITIOUS FOOD SUPPLY AND OPTIMIZE AGRICULTURE PRODUCTION, VALUECHAIN AND SERVE STAKEHOLDERS. NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP: ISU RESEARCHERS ARE DEVELOPING TOOLS AND STRATEGIES THAT CONSERVE NATURAL RESOURCES AND PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT, AND IDENTIFYING FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH DISEASE THAT WILL ENHANCE THE MANAGEMENT AND CONSERVATION OF WILDLIFE POPULATIONS AND PROTECT HUMAN HEALTH. SOIL FERTILITY RESEARCH IS BEING CONDUCTED TO UNDERSTAND UNDERLYING PROCESSES THAT INFLUENCE SOIL ACIDIFICATION, CROP PHOSPHORUS AND POTASSIUM NEEDS AND UPTAKE, IMPACTS OF HARVEST AND RECYCLING TO THE SOIL, AND TRANSPORT OF SOIL COMPONENTS OFF FIELD, AS WELL AS EFFICIENT METHODS OF NUTRIENT OR AMENDMENTS APPLICATION. HEALTH, NUTRITION, AND WELL-BEING: ISU RESEARCHERS ARE STUDYING WAYS TO IMPROVE HUMAN HEALTH THROUGH INFORMING CONSUMERS ABOUT NUTRITION AND LIFESTYLE APPROACHES, AND DEVELOPMENT OF A FOOD SYSTEM THAT IS COST-EFFICIENT AND NUTRIENT RICH. SCIENTISTS ARE CONDUCTING STUDIES TO IDENTIFY NEW TARGETS THAT COULD STRENGTHEN THE IMMUNE SYSTEM TO PREVENT INFECTIOUS DISEASES TO IMPROVE WELL-BEING OF ANIMALS, PREVENT ZOONOTIC DISEASES THAT IMPACT HUMANS AND REDUCE THE CHANCES OF FUTURE DISEASE OUTBREAKS. OTHER WORK IS IDENTIFYING NOVEL GENES IMPORTANT FOR IMMUNE FUNCTION TO ADVANCE GENETIC SELECTION OF DOMESTICATED ANIMALS WITH DESIRABLE TRAITS. HUMAN POTENTIAL AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, AND COMMUNITY AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT: ISU SCIENTISTS ARE WORKING TO ENHANCE THE RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION OF STUDENTS INTO AGRICULTURAL FIELDS TO ENSURE A SUSTAINABLE WORKFORCE. PROJECTS FOCUS ON FAMILIES AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE AND SUSTAINABILITY, AND OPTIMIZING QUALITY OF LIFE ACROSS THE LIFESPAN. TRANSFORMATIVE TECHN OLOGY: ISU RESEARCHERS ARE DEVELOPING MACHINE SYSTEMS TO SUSTAINABLY INTENSIFY AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION TO MEET GLOBAL FOOD DEMAND. OVERALL, THE RESEARCH WILL IMPROVE THE MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY OF AGRARIAN AND INTENSIVELY MANAGED LANDSCAPES AND CONTRIBUTE TO BROADER SOCIALLY RELEVANT OUTCOMES THAT INCLUDE INCREASED ECONOMIC COMPETITIVENESS OF THE US AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISE. TARGET AUDIENCES AND OUTCOMES: THESE PROJECTS ARE OF HIGH VALUE TO A WIDE RANGE OF AUDIENCES. INFORMATION FROM THIS RESEARCH IS WIDELY DISSEMINATED THROUGH MANY OUTLETS. OUR GOAL IS TO BUILD THE CAPACITY OF ISU'S RESEARCH PROGRAMS TO MEET THE DEMANDS OF AGRICULTURE WHILE ENSURING QUALITY OF LIFE FOR CITIZENS, BUILDING PRODUCTIVE AG-COMMUNITIES, PROTECTING NATURAL RESOURCES AND THE ENVIRONMENT, APPLYING TECHNOLOGY APPROPRIATELY AND EFFECTIVELY, AND GENERATING NEW KNOWLEDGE. ISU RESEARCHERS STRIVE TO OPTIMIZE THE USE OF CAPACITY FUNDS THROUGH THEIR RESEARCH BY ADDRESSING RELEVANT AND CRITICAL ISSUES FOR OUR STATE, REGION AND NATION.

NOTABLE OUTCOMES INCLUDE THE DEVELOPMENT OF DROUGHT- AND DISEASE RESISTANT CROP VARIETIES, IMPROVED MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT ENHANCE SOIL HEALTH AND WATER USE  EFFICIENCY, AND NEW TECHNOLOGIES FOR PEST AND DISEASE CONTROL. THESE EFFORTS HAVE RESULTED IN INCREASED  YIELDS, REDUCED INPUT COSTS, AND MORE RESILIENT CROPPING SYSTEMS FOR TEXAS PRODUCERS. RESEARCH ON FOOD  SAFETY, ANIMAL HEALTH, AND LIVESTOCK MANAGEMENT HAS ALSO CONTRIBUTED TO IMPROVED PUBLIC HEALTH AND  GREATER PROFITABILITY FOR AGRICULTURAL STAKEHOLDERS. IN FY23, THE COLLEGE OF MICRONESIA LAND GRANT PROGRAM WILL CONTINUE TO ADDRESS THE FOLLOWING SIX CRITICAL ISSUES:  1. LACK OF LOCAL FOOD PRODUCTION AND FOOD INSECURITY: AGRICULTURE IS ESSENTIAL FOR SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND FOOD SECURITY OF SMALL ISLAND COMMUNITIES IN MICRONESIA. THIS PROGRAM WILL ADDRESS VARIOUS ISSUES IN SUSTAINABLE PLANT AND ANIMAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS AND THEIR IMPLICATIONS ON MICRONESIAN ISLANDS ENVIRONMENT, INCLUDING ATOLLS. EMPHASIS WILL BE PLACED ON TRADITIONAL FOOD PRODUCTION SYSTEMS, CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES, TECHNIQUES THAT INTEGRATE CONVENTIONAL PRACTICES WITH CONTEMPORARY APPROACHES, AND PROCESSING AND MARKETING CROPS AND ANIMAL PRODUCTS.  2. SUSTAINABLE AQUACULTURE DEVELOPMENT: THERE IS GROWING EMPHASIS ON THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF MARINE RESOURCES TO MEET THE FUTURE ECONOMIC NEEDS OF THE ISLAND NATIONS, PROVIDE SELFSUFFICIENCY, AND IMPROVE THE FOOD AND FINANCIAL SECURITY OF ISLAND COMMUNITIES. THE DEVELOPMENT OF HATCHERYBASED AQUACULTURE PRODUCTION HAS GREAT POTENTIAL TO ADDRESS ISSUES RELATED TO THE DECLINE IN NATURAL POPULATIONS OF ECONOMICALLY IMPORTANT MARINE SPECIES. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS WILL FOCUS ON AQUACULTURE SPECIES, INCLUDING GIANT CLAM, MILKFISH, RABBITFISH, SEA CUCUMBER, AND MANGROVE CRABS. ESTABLISHING SITESPECIFIC HATCHERY TECHNIQUES FOR THESE SPECIES WILL HELP IN STOCK ENHANCEMENT.  3. YOUTH AND FAMILY ISSUES IN THE COMMUNITIES: THE MULTITUDE OF PROBLEMS THAT MICRONESIAN YOUTH FACE IN PRESENTDAY LIFE MUST BE ADDRESSED WITH PROGRAMS AND PRACTICAL STRATEGIES TO RESTORE AND PRESERVE THE AUTHENTIC MICRONESIAN CULTURE AND TRADITIONS. SUCH PROGRAMS WILL EVENTUALLY BRING OPPORTUNITIES FOR INCOME GENERATION, ENTREPRENEURIAL SKILLS, AND MORAL VALUE IMPROVEMENT. YOUTH PROGRAMS WILL CONTINUE TO SERVE YOUTH BY PROVIDING EDUCATIONAL WORKSHOPS ON ACQUIRING KNOWLEDGE AND DEVELOPING LIFELONG SKILLS, FORMING POSITIVE ADULT RELATIONSHIPS, AND LEADERSHIP EXPERIENCES. LEADERSHIP AND VOLUNTEERISM, CIVIC, ECONOMIC, AND CULTURAL SKILL PROGRAMS ARE ESSENTIAL FOR THE FAMILY, YOUTH, AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT ENDEAVORS.  4. CLIMATE CHALLENGES IN MICRONESIA: SMALL ISLAND AGRICULTURE SYSTEMS ARE HIGHLY VULNERABLE, AFFECTING FOOD SECURITY, LIVELIHOODS, AND ECONOMIC PROSPERITY. ENHANCING LOCAL COMMUNITIES ADAPTIVE CAPACITY IS CRITICAL TO FOOD AND NUTRITION SECURITY GOALS. DEVELOPING LOCALLY SUITABLE CLIMATERESILIENT FOOD SYSTEMS IS UNEXPLORED IN RESEARCH AND PRACTICE. ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE VARIABILITY AND EXTREME EVENTS SERVES AS A BASIS FOR REDUCING VULNERABILITY TO LONGTERM CLIMATE CHANGE. PROGRAMS UNDER THIS CRITICAL ISSUE WILL ENABLE COMMUNITIES TO ADOPT SITESPECIFIC AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION METHODS AND PRACTICES.  5. FOOD CONTAMINATION AND RESULTING FOODBORNE ILLNESSES ARE GROWING CONCERNS ACROSS THE MICRONESIAN REGION. THE PROGRAM WILL EDUCATE AND TRAIN THE TARGET AUDIENCE TO INCREASE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS, ENSURE SAFE FOOD PREPARATION, HANDLING, AND STORAGE, ADOPT BEST PRACTICES,IMPROVE THEQUALITY AND SAFETY OF FOOD PRODUCTS, AND REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF FOODBORNE AND WATERBORNE ILLNESSES. IT WILL ALSO CONTINUE STRENGTHENING EXISTING COLLABORATIONS ON PROGRAMS THAT INFORM STAKEHOLDERS ABOUT HEALTHY LIFESTYLES AND THE CONSUMPTION OF SAFE AND HEALTHY FOODS.  6. CHILDHOOD OBESITY: THE PROGRAMS UNDER THIS CRITICAL ISSUE WILL PROMOTE CHILDRENS WELLBEING THROUGH ACTIVE PROGRAMS AND PROVIDE INFORMATION ABOUT NUTRITION, HEALTH, PHYSICAL EDUCATION, AND APPROPRIATE INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE AND PRACTICES. ACTIVITIES WILL PROMOTE SPORTS AND EXERCISE, SCHOOL, HOME, AND COMMUNITY GARDENING ACTIVITIES TO ENCOURAGE AND INCREASE LOCAL FRUITS AND VEGETABLES AMONG STUDENTS WITH ACTIVITIES SUCH AS PROPER MEAL PLANNING TO ADDRESS OBESITY.  THE COMLG EXTENSION PROGRAMS AND RESEARCH PROJECTS FOCUS ON ISSUES PERTINENT TO EACH LOCATION WHILE TARGETING TO ACHIEVE THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE ENTIRE MICRONESIAN REGIONS CRITICAL ISSUES
